why.text: An Atlantic coastal strip north of the Tejo estuary, with clay-limestone and clay-sand soils, humid west winds and dry summers, and a very wide range of grapes.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosés, plus sparkling wine, fortified (licoroso) wine and a low-alcohol Lisboa Leve.

climate.text: A transition between the zone of humid, constant west winds and dry summers, with an Atlantic coastal strip.

soil.text: Very varied: limestone and marl, sandstone, Mediterranean clays, podzols, sands, alluvium and basalt clays. Mostly clay-limestone and clay-sand formations.

tastes.text: Whites: lemon-yellow, fruity, aromatic, some persistence. Reds: red, violet or garnet, aromatic, full-bodied, strong, improve with age. Lisboa Leve: low alcohol, fruity or floral, fresh and slightly tart.

styles.name: Lisboa Leve
styles.text: Light wine, at most 10% alcohol, fruity or floral, fresh and slightly tart.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine made only by the classic method, at least 11% alcohol.

styles.name: Vinho licoroso
styles.text: Fortified wine, 15 to 22% alcohol, from must of at least 12% natural strength.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional term allowed on labels, with Garrafeira, Superior and Colheita Seleccionada.

why.text: Vines grow in sand over deep clay close to the Atlantic, with sea winds and a mild, humid summer. Sea, winds and soil together spared them from phylloxera.

styles.text: Red and white wines only; the red is aged 18 months in vessel plus 6 in bottle, the white 6 plus 3.

climate.text: Strong Atlantic maritime influence, with sea winds and a mild, humid summer.

soil.text: Two soils: sandy ground over consolidated material ("chão de areia"), and brown limestone marl soils ("chão rijo"). Deep clay lies under the sand.

tastes.text: Whites are lemon to straw-gold, light fruity. Reds are ruby to garnet; Ramisco is astringent but softens with age. Balanced, with a complex finish and tannins and acids fused.

styles.name: Colares red
styles.text: Minimum 10% alcohol; 18 months in vessel then 6 months in bottle before sale.

styles.name: Colares white
styles.text: Minimum 10% alcohol; 6 months in vessel then 3 months in bottle before sale.

why.text: A tiny coastal area near the Tagus mouth, with a mild Mediterranean climate, mostly limy soils and plots facing south-west, making smooth fortified wine aged in wood.

styles.text: Fortified (licoroso) wine, white or red, with 15 to 22% alcohol and up to 150 g/l residual sugar.

climate.text: Mild Mediterranean climate without big temperature swings, because the sea is close.

soil.text: Red Mediterranean soils on normal limestone, normal limestone soils, and reddish-brown non-calcareous clays; some plots are stony.

tastes.text: Delicate and velvety, with a slightly almond aroma. Whites run straw-yellow to deep gold, reds ruby to topaz. Ageing makes the perfume stronger and the colour paler.

styles.name: Vinho generoso
styles.text: Fortified Carcavelos; at least two years in wood and six months in bottle.

why.text: Poor marl and hard limestone soils on the slopes of the Trancão river valley, with cold winters and mild summers, shape fresh, acidic whites made mostly from Arinto.

styles.text: Mostly dry to soft whites, with reds allowed and sparkling wine made by the bottle-fermentation method.

climate.text: A typical microclimate, quite cold in winter and mild in summer; the valleys are narrow and enclosed by high hills.

soil.text: Poor soils, mostly from marls and hard limestones (the traditional "caeiras"), as a rule deep and with coarse material.

tastes.text: Whites are citrus-coloured, fruity and lightly acidic, dry to soft; with age they turn golden with complex tertiary aromas. Sparkling wines are very fruity and fresh, with a fine, persistent bubble.

styles.name: Arinto blend
styles.text: Bucelas wine must contain at least 75% Arinto.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine made only by classic bottle fermentation, base wine must qualify as Bucelas.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional mention allowed on the label, along with Garrafeira, Superior and Escolha.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Traditional mention allowed on the label for Bucelas wines.

why.text: Mild Atlantic-influenced climate, clay-limestone soils and about 700 mm of rain: fresh fruity whites on low coastal ground, full-bodied reds in the inland hills.

styles.text: Still red and white wines only; the white zone is wider and nearer the coast, the red zone is in the inland hills.

climate.text: Mild, without big temperature swings; Mediterranean traits with Atlantic influence. Average rainfall is 700 mm a year.

soil.text: Mostly clay-limestone, brown and red, with clayey, sandy-clay or loamy texture. Often shallow and of low fertility.

tastes.text: Whites: fruity and aromatic, fresh with a slight tartness, from the Atlantic influence. Reds: garnet, intense winey aroma, a little astringent when young, becoming soft, elegant and velvety with age.

why.text: Limestone and Mediterranean soils on hillsides and in valleys, with mountains to the north and west that hold back the Atlantic and let in Mediterranean sun, tempered by Atlantic mists and summer breezes.

styles.text: Red and white wines only.

climate.text: Mountains to the north and west block Atlantic influence and let the Mediterranean in. Mediterranean sun gives easy ripening and alcoholic strength, while Atlantic mists and summer breezes balance sugar build-up and acid loss with the forming of aromas and phenolic compounds.

soil.text: Brown or red Mediterranean soils from fine sandstone, sands or claystone, and brown or red limestone soils from marl and fine sandstone.

tastes.text: Whites: aromatic, full and persistent, showing Mediterranean ripening, colour citrus to golden straw. Reds: winey, lively and bright when young; intense and balanced with rare bouquet when aged, ruby to garnet.

why.text: Hills and knolls running from the Serra de Montejunto towards Óbidos, on loam to clayey limestone soils, give fresh, fruity wines.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, plus white sparkling wine made by the classic bottle-fermentation method.

soil.text: Loam to clayey soils of brown and red limestone, or brown and red Mediterranean soils from non-limestone material.

tastes.text: Whites: lemon-coloured, fresh, aromatic and balanced, with fruity and floral notes and light mineral touches. Reds: open in colour, ruby, fruity, soft, with some body. Sparkling whites: fine lasting foam, fine fruity aroma, good balance of acidity and freshness.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: White sparkling wine made by the classic method, with fermentation in the bottle.

why.text: Hillside vineyards with an Atlantic maritime climate on brown limestone or marl-and-sandstone soils give aromatic, lightly acidic whites and soft, velvety reds.

styles.text: Red and white table wines only.

soil.text: Brown limestone soils, or marl and fine sandstone parent-rock soils, with exposure good for quality wine.

tastes.text: Whites: aromatic, lightly fruity, with a slight acidity. Reds: velvety and soft, and they develop early.
